subject: Nanotechnology
title: Metal-Organic Frameworks
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Metal-Organic Frameworks.

hook.text: A teaspoon of MOF powder has the internal surface area of a football field — self-assembled sponges at the nanoscale.

buildup.text: Metal ions and organic linkers self-assemble into crystalline frameworks with tunable pore size and chemistry.

discovery.text: Over 100,000 MOF structures have been reported — each designed by choosing different metals and linkers.

twist.text: MOFs are fragile — water, acid, and mechanical stress can collapse the framework. Stability remains the biggest challenge.

climax.text: MOFs capture CO₂ from air, store hydrogen for fuel cells, and deliver drugs — all from self-assembled crystals.

punchline.text: The most porous materials ever made build themselves — one metal node at a time.

quiz.question: Why do metal-organic frameworks have such enormous surface areas?
options: They contain millions of sharp spikes at the nanoscale
Self-assembled crystalline pores create vast internal cavities accessible to molecules
They expand when exposed to air, increasing their external surface
